newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein leaves Jordan for talks with Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein leaves Jordan for talks with Mubarak.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan left Amman on Tuesday for the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh for talks with President Hosni Mubarak, witnesses said.

Jordanian officials said the two leaders would try to find ways to bridge gaps between Israeli and Palestinian negotiators who have yet to seal an accord on a long overdue Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
"The meeting is aimed at coordination and moving the peace process forward," one official said of the meeting, agreed in a telephone call late on Monday.

King Hussein, regarded as Israel's closest Arab ally since Jordan signed a peace treaty with the Jewish state in 1994, has expressed anxiety about renewed violence in the region if Israel does not honour its peace accords with the Palestinians.

On Sunday he urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat to agree on the Hebron redeployment so they could move ahead with implementation of an interim Palestinian self-rule accord.
